title: Write against the canonical piece
statement: Make one component canonical and write the rest against it: list what later components may not re-ask, and let none of them contradict it.
example: One lesson design lists the two questions its film asks and the two words the film defines as off-limits for re-asking.
detail: The lesson-components spec makes the background film canonical: no later component may contradict it or re-ask its questions. Each lesson design then lists what is off-limits for re-asking, such as the film's sync checks, its stamped definitions and naming the story pattern in the abstract, and a rebuilt lesson keeps the same discipline: glossed words and sync-checked answers are never re-asked. It is the across-components form of telling a writer what an earlier block covers.
